correctness.rationale: The product rule gives an independently checked nonzero-power criterion height≥(j−1)|shift|. Integer counting yields the exact cumulative numerator and total population. The real parameter body has volume (n−1)^3/3, and two exact polynomial integrals give the harmonic and ideal-height tails. The discrete-to-continuous limit uses a uniform monotone-sum error O(1/N); a tail-sum bound proves logarithmic finite expectation. Repeated multiplication for every admissible integer triple through N=18 and exact rational cross-checks corroborate critical identities.

value.rationale: The paper-defined real inverse monoid has unbounded but individually finite nilpotency indices. The previously unquantified natural Lebesgue/counting sampling reveals an exact universal harmonic law with infinite mean, whereas uniformly sampled finite-grid elements have mean growing logarithmically. The explicit cumulative finite census and ideal-dependent tail coefficient measure how this behavior persists across every nontrivial principal ideal. These are structural, naturally motivated distributional invariants rather than a chosen isolated coefficient.
